# Promoted to repo memory: commit-attribution

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `commit-attribution M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-13T08:02:19.961Z) — `sofar new <slug>` binds the current branch by default, silently replacing whatever binding that branch already had. On a repo like this one — where main carries a live initiative and several sessions share the worktree — that knocks the in-flight initiative off the branch peer sessions and hooks resolve through, with no warning. Check `.sofar/bindings.json` before running it; pass `--no-bind` when the current branch is already bound to live work, then reach the new record with `sofar switch <slug>` or a dedicated branch.
- **M2** (2026-08-13T08:12:05.394Z) — Trailer probe results, git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), run 2026-08-13 before D4 was taken. Read incantation: `git log --format='%h|%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. Always pass `separator=` — bare `valueonly` emits a TRAILING NEWLINE that corrupts any line-oriented parse.

Survival: cherry-pick PRESERVES the trailer; rebase PRESERVES it (rebase is a cherry-pick sequence); a commit with no trailer reads back as an empty field, never as a guess.

KNOWN LOSSY PATH — squash merge. `git merge --squash` writes SQUASH_MSG with each original message INDENTED BY FOUR SPACES, so git's trailer parser does not see it and the squashed commit reads back as empty. Committing with `-m` discards SQUASH_MSG entirely and loses it the same way. The slug text is still present verbatim in the body, so a fallback that scans the body for an indented marker recovers it exactly — still reading git, not guessing. Consequence if unhandled: a squash-merged initiative reads as "not shipped" when it did ship — a FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the safe direction but still wrong. Not an issue while this repo commits straight to main; it becomes one the first time work lands through a squashed PR.
- **M3** (2026-08-13T08:19:56.315Z) — Claude Code exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID into the agent's shell, and its value is EXACTLY the session id sofar registers (verified 2026-08-13 against a live session: env value matched the injected "Session: <id>" line character for character). Critically, git hooks INHERIT it — a probe prepare-commit-msg hook wrote the live session id into a commit message. That is what makes automatic, exact commit attribution possible from a process that has no access to the MCP server's in-memory pin: resolve the env var through homeInitiative (mcp/context.ts:174, already imported by cli/event.ts) rather than through bindings.json.

Related vars present in the same environment: CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION.

CAVEAT: none of these are a documented contract — they are Claude Code implementation details and can disappear in any release. Anything depending on them must degrade to silence, never to a branch-binding guess (D5's standing rule), and the silence must be visible or the signal rots without anyone noticing.
- **M4** (2026-08-13T08:38:21.531Z) — VERSION SKEW makes commit attribution a silent no-op, and nothing currently reports it. The prepare-commit-msg shim guards with `command -v sofar`, which succeeds for ANY installed sofar — including one too old to have the `commit-trailer` subcommand. The unknown subcommand then fails, `|| true` swallows it, and the hook exits 0. Result: the hook is installed, every commit looks normal, and nothing is ever attributed.

Confirmed live on 2026-08-13: the sofar on PATH here is 0.25.1, which predates `commit-trailer`, so installing the hook in this repo TODAY would attribute nothing until a release carrying the command is published and installed. Verified by running `sofar commit-trailer --help` against the global binary — it fell through to top-level help rather than the subcommand.

This is the concrete form of the exposure task 2.5(b) names: silence is the correct behaviour per D5, but invisible silence rots. The safety net is 2.4's doctor check (commits on the branch carrying no trailer), which is NOT built yet. Until it is, assume attribution is off unless a commit has been verified to carry the trailer.
- **M5** (2026-08-13T09:57:28.684Z) — sofar_end_session is the ONLY write tool with no `initiative` parameter. log_decision, update_task, update_plan, add_note, remember and close_initiative all accept one and route by it; end_session accepts only session_id, summary and next_action, so its write-back ALWAYS follows the session pin.

Consequence, observed live on 2026-08-13: a session working an initiative its branch is not bound to can route every decision, task update and note correctly by passing `initiative` explicitly, and still have every write-back land in the WRONG record. This session was pinned to drift-certification (main's binding) while doing all its work in commit-attribution, so ~10 write-backs describing commit-attribution work are filed in drift-certification's session files, and doctor reports the session as spanning two initiatives.

Working around it costs nothing but must be deliberate: state the true subject in the first clause of every summary ("No X work; this session ran entirely in Y"), and preserve the pinned initiative's real next_action rather than overwriting it with your own — otherwise the branch owner's next action is silently replaced.

The clean avoidance is to give the initiative its own branch so the binding resolves to it. `--no-bind` is correct when the current branch already carries live work, but it leaves this asymmetry exposed for the whole session.
- **M6** (2026-08-13T10:04:44.480Z) — RE-HOMING A SESSION mid-flight already works and is the correct move whenever a session starts working an initiative its branch is not bound to: call sofar_start_session with BOTH session_id and an explicit `initiative`. It appends a later session_started, and homeInitiative resolves by the LATEST registration across every log (record-integrity D13), so the session re-homes while bindings.json is untouched and every other live session on the old initiative is unaffected.

Demonstrated live 2026-08-13 on this session: the statusline went from "drift-certification 15/25" to "commit-attribution 15/24 (2 dropped)" after one re-home call, with bindings.json unchanged and three peer drift-certification sessions unaffected. Every surface follows, because they all resolve session-first through resolveSessionFirst — statusline (cli/statusline.ts:204), the SessionStart digest, and the hooks.

WHY SESSIONS GET THIS WRONG: the installed protocol block says only "Do still call sofar_start_session, passing the session_id from the injected context line". It never says to ALSO pass `initiative` when the work moves to a different record, so an agent adopts the branch's initiative and stays mis-homed for its whole life — routing individual writes correctly with explicit `initiative` args while every write-back lands in the wrong log, since sofar_end_session is the one write tool that cannot be targeted and always follows the pin.

The rule of thumb: passing `initiative` on a write routes THAT write; re-homing via start_session moves the SESSION. If more than one or two writes are going somewhere other than the pinned record, re-home instead.
- **M7** (2026-08-13T10:22:14.493Z) — RELEASE GATE, ruled by the user 2026-08-13: do NOT publish a new sofar.sh version until this initiative is finished. Let the whole thing land, then publish once.

Why it is worth obeying rather than shipping incrementally. Attribution is a CHAIN — the prepare-commit-msg hook writes the trailer, core/attribution.ts reads it, doctor reports whether it is working, and the shipping notice and review packet consume it. Publishing a partial chain puts users in the worst state available: the hook installs and writes trailers while some consumer is missing, or doctor reports "attribution off" in a version that has no way to turn it on. The current repo state is the honest one BECAUSE nothing is published — the PATH binary is 0.25.1, predates commit-trailer, so the hook is deliberately not installed and doctor says so accurately.

Two consequences for any session working here. First, do not install the prepare-commit-msg hook in this repo before the release; trailers stay hand-written until then, and doctor's accurate "attribution off" is more useful than a misleading "installed but nothing attributed". Second, session-orientation's protocol-block change rides the same release — protocol blocks are a versioned ledger and a half-shipped one leaves repos matching no known version, so that initiative's Phase 1 is part of what must land before publishing.

Publishing itself remains the user's action (they run `npm publish -w sofar.sh` for the classifier and OTP), so this gate is about not ASKING for it early, not about permission.
- **M8** (2026-08-13T10:23:17.508Z) — SUPERSEDES the squash caveat in the 2026-08-13 trailer-probe memory: `git merge --squash` no longer loses attribution. core/attribution.ts scans the body for the INDENTED trailer a squash leaves behind, so a squashed commit reads back with its slug(s) (D16). What that probe memory says about the MECHANISM is still exactly right — SQUASH_MSG indents each original message four spaces, which is why git's own trailer parser sees nothing — only its "not handled" conclusion is stale.

Still unrecoverable BY CONSTRUCTION, and not a gap to close later: committing a squash with `-m` or `-F` discards SQUASH_MSG entirely, so the slug is not in the commit object at all and there is nothing to read.

Diagnosing this family of bugs without a real push: the live shipping signal keeps a per-session mark of origin/<branch> at `.sofar/.index/shipwatch.json` (gitignored, disposable). Rewind that mark to an older sha and run `echo '{"session_id":"<id>"}' | node packages/engine/dist/cli.js event user-prompt` — the handler then walks `<old>..<current>` against real repo history and prints exactly what a live session would see. Deleting the file resets the signal; it is a cache, never truth.

TEST TRAP that cost a cycle here: writing a commit-message file INSIDE the repo work tree gets it staged by the next `git add -A`, and the checkout back to the base branch then aborts with "local changes would be overwritten". Write message files outside the work tree.
